---
title: "Week 9: Children Are Not Collateral Damage"
---

## Theme: Child Health: Lead, ACEs, School Environments, and Cumulative
Harm

Adverse childhood experiences --- abuse, neglect, household dysfunction,
and exposure to community violence --- are among the strongest known
predictors of adult physical and mental health. They are also
distributed by ZIP code. New research by Barboza-Salerno et al. (2026)
advances an environmental justice framework that moves beyond
individual-level social disadvantage to examine how neighborhood
conditions predict child maltreatment risk.

## Classroom Lab Demonstration

**Legal Focus:** Child welfare law and mandatory reporting obligations
under CAPTA (Child Abuse Prevention and Treatment Act); NEPA and
children\'s environmental health protections; Individuals with
Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) and school safety mandates; Title IV-E
foster care funding and its relationship to neighborhood poverty.

**Health Focus:** ACEs (adverse childhood experiences) as cumulative
risk factors for adult cardiovascular disease, cancer, substance use
disorder, and early death; the dose-response relationship between ACE
score and adult health outcomes; environmental toxin exposure (lead, air
pollution) as an additional ACE-like stressor.

**Data:** K-12 School Shooting Database (SSDB, k12ssdb.org); NCES school
location shapefiles
(nces.ed.gov/programs/edge/geographic/schoollocations); CDC Social
Vulnerability Index 2020; EPA EJScreen (ejscreen.epa.gov); Area
Deprivation Index from Neighborhood Atlas
(neighborhoodatlas.medicine.wisc.edu); county-level ACE prevalence from
CDC BRFSS.

**R Code:** Load school shooting CSV from k12ssdb.org; join to NCES
school shapefile by NCESSCH school ID; sf::st_buffer() at 500m around
schools; sf::st_join() to identify schools within industrial buffers
from Week 7; scale() to standardize ADI, SVI, and EJScreen components;
rowMeans() to compute composite vulnerability index.

- Import K-12 School Shooting Database (k12ssdb.org) and NCES school
  location shapefiles into QGIS

- Create spatial overlay: identify schools within 500m of industrial
  sites using buffers from Week 7 lab

- Join with ADI, SVI, and county-level ACE prevalence data in R;
  construct a composite child vulnerability index by census tract using
  standardized z-scores

- Map composite index by census tract; identify top 10 highest-burden
  tracts in Franklin County

- Apply Barboza-Salerno et al. (2026) EJ framework: add EJScreen
  particulate matter and proximity-to-hazardous-sites variables; test
  whether adding EJ indicators changes which tracts rank highest
